## Commands

`always` runs on every `verify` and every close; `milestone` runs on the baseline,
`verify --full` and a top-level task's close — a subtask's close is quick. Mark a slow
command `milestone` so the inner loop and subtask closes stay short.

| Action | Command | When |
|---|---|---|
| install | npm install | always |
| build | npm run build | milestone |
| typecheck | npm run typecheck | always |
| lint | npm run lint | always |

`build` is `prisma generate && next build`: it regenerates the Prisma client, so it is the
row that must run before anything that consumes generated types. It is `milestone` because
it costs a full Turbopack compile.

`install` is declared but not executed by `verify` — the kit only runs build, typecheck,
lint and test. It is here so a session knows the install command when `node_modules` is
missing.

Repo scripts that are not part of the suite (`package.json`):

| Script | Command | Use |
|---|---|---|
| `dev` | `next dev` | local server on :3000 |
| `start` | `next start` | serve the built output |
| `radio:seed` | `node --experimental-strip-types prisma/seed/seed-radio.mts` | seed featured radio categories |
| `radio:backfill` | `node --experimental-strip-types prisma/seed/backfill-radio-groups.mts` | backfill station groups |
| `postinstall` | `prisma generate` | fires automatically on install |

The `.mts` seed scripts run under Node's type stripping, which is why `tsconfig.json`
sets `allowImportingTsExtensions`.

## Entry points

- `src/app/layout.tsx` — root layout: metadata, fonts, and the provider stack every
  route inherits (theme, radio player, spatial nav, watch sync, wishlist, toaster).
- `src/app/page.tsx` — the home shell, composed against `getActiveThemeState()`.
- `src/proxy.ts` — the Next.js 16 request interceptor (renamed from `middleware`), which
  refreshes the Supabase session through `src/lib/supabase/middleware.ts`.
- `src/app/api/health/route.ts`, `src/app/api/push/run/route.ts`,
  `src/app/api/radio/resolve/route.ts` — the HTTP route handlers.
- `src/app/actions/*.ts` — the `"use server"` Server Action modules.
- `prisma/schema.prisma` — the data model all of the above reads through `src/lib/db.ts`.

## Detection notes

- **No test script.** Confirmed correct, not a detection miss: there is no test runner in
  `package.json` and no test file in the tree. Do not invent a `test` row; add one only
  when a runner is actually installed.
- The detector guessed `install: npm install` from the lockfile. It is correct, with the
  caveat above that `verify` does not run it.

## Domain notes

- **Supabase Auth ids are the join key.** `Profile.id` is the Supabase auth user id;
  `src/lib/auth.ts` upserts the row rather than creating a second identity. There is no
  separate user table.
- **Two clients, one database.** Supabase owns auth and the browser session; Prisma owns
  every table query. Reads go through `src/lib/db.ts` (a pooled singleton, cached on
  `globalThis` outside production); nothing issues SQL directly.
- **The theme is resolved server-side, once per request.** `getActiveThemeState()`
  (`src/lib/theme/active.ts`) is the single source of truth for which theme and which
  experience a request renders; the layout paints it and pages compose against it. The
  visitor's choice lives in a cookie (`k79_theme_state`), the published default lives in
  Postgres, and the studio choice outranks the published one.
- **Many reads are deliberately local-first.** Watch progress and radio favourites work
  signed out, persist through `src/lib/safeStorage.ts` (which falls back to an in-memory
  map when a WebView blocks `localStorage`), and reconcile to Postgres in the background.
  A server-only fix for those features breaks the signed-out path.
- **Radio hydrates on demand.** Only featured categories are seeded; opening any other one
  fetches its upstream playlist, dedupes by stream URL, caps at 400 stations and writes to
  Postgres. An empty category in a fresh database is expected, not a bug.
- **Deployment is self-hosted as well as Vercel.** `next.config.ts` sets
  `output: "standalone"` for the Dockerfile, and the image loader is custom so images
  never route through Vercel's metered optimizer. `SITE_URL` is read before
  `NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL` because `NEXT_PUBLIC_*` is baked in at build time.
- **Committed build artifacts exist on purpose.** `releases/cinevo.apk`, `cinevo.msi` and
  `app-release-*.apk` are release outputs, not workspace noise. Leave them alone unless a
  release task says otherwise.
